name: 黃如瑩
objective:
This course aims to understand and analyze contemporary popular English fiction, including novels, novellas and stories, and their film adaptations. It seeks to enhance students’ language proficiency, cross-cultural awareness, and artistic appreciation. Through class discussions, the course also encourages students’ interest and effectiveness in acquiring language abilities and cross-cultural intelligences.
Course activities include:  
(1) Weekly guided reading and introduction of a popular novel (or series), with selected passages read in the original text and related film scenes viewed in class;  
(2) Each student selects a popular novel of their choice and gives two oral presentations: one before the midterm and one before the final exam. In the final project, students present their own analysis or creative reinterpretation.
本課程目的在於了解並分析當今正在流行的英語小說 (或長短篇故事) 與其改編的電影，以充實同學的語文程度，跨文化素養與藝術涵養，並截由討論促進同學學習語言文化的興趣與效能。課程進行內容為 (1) 教授每周導讀並引介一本 (或一套) 流行小說，帶領學生閱讀原文小說精彩節選並觀賞改編電影精彩片段，(2) 每位同學選擇一本自己喜歡的流行小說，期中考前與期末考前作兩次口頭報告，並在 (3) 期末書面報告呈現自己的解析或是再創作.
schedule:
Syllabus:
Week 1: Course Introduction
(1) Introduction to course goals, requirements, and assessment.  
(2) Overview of contemporary popular fiction and film adaptation.  

Unit One: The World of a Child’s Heart  
Week 2: The Tale of Peter Rabbit 彼得兔的故事 by Beatrix Potter
(1) Reading: Selected passages from “The Tale of Peter Rabbit” and related animal stories
(2) Film: Selected clips from an animated or live-action adaptation.  
(3) Focus: Childhood curiosity, mischief, and moral lessons.  

Week 3: The BFG 吹夢巨人 by Roald Dahl
(1) Reading: Selected chapters from “The BFG.”
(2) Film: Selected clips from the film adaptation.  
(3) Focus: Child–adult relationships, imagination, and language play.  

Week 4: Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland 愛麗絲夢遊仙境 by Lewis Carroll
(1) Reading: Key episodes from “Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland”
(2) Film: Selected clips from major film adaptations
(3) Focus: Nonsense, fantasy, and the child’s perspective on adult rules.  

Unit Two: The Bravery of a Young Adult  
Week 5: The Maze Runner Series 移動迷宮系列 by James Dashner
(1) Reading: Selected chapters from “The Maze Runner”
(2) Film: Selected scenes from the film adaptation.  
(3) Focus: Survival, leadership, and dystopian control.  

Week 6: The Divergent Series 分歧者系 by Veronica Roth
(1) Reading: Selected chapters from “Divergent”
(2) Film: Key scenes from the film adaptation.  
(3) Focus: Identity, faction systems, and resistance.  

Week 7: The Hunger Games Series 飢餓遊戲系列 by Suzanne Collins
(1) Reading: Selected chapters from “The Hunger Games”
(2) Film: Selected scenes from the film adaptation.  
(3) Focus: Spectacle, violence, and political oppression.  

Week 8: The Fault in Our Stars 生命中的美好缺憾 by John Green
(1) Reading: Selected chapters from “The Fault in Our Stars”
(2) Film: Selected scenes from the film adaptation
(3) Focus: Illness, love, and the meaning of an “ordinary” life

Week 9: Midterm Presentations on the 1st half of student-chosen novel
(1) Each student presents the first half of their chosen contemporary popular Anglo/American novel.  
(2) Content: Author background, brief plot overview, main characters, and initial themes.  
(3) Format: 5 minute oral presentation plus Q&A (time may be adjusted).  

Unit Three: The Strengths of an Adult  
Week 10: The Danish Girl 丹麥女孩 by David Ebershoff
(1) Reading: Selected chapters from “The Danish Girl”
(2) Film: Selected scenes from the film adaptation
(3) Focus: Gender identity, marriage, and self-discovery.  

Week 11: The King’s Speech 王者之聲 by Mark Logue & Peter Conradi
(1) Reading: Selected chapters from “The King’s Speech: How One Man Saved the British Monarchy”
(2) Film: Key scenes from the film adaptation.  
(3) Focus: Disability, public voice, and political responsibility.  

Week 12: The Silver Linings Playbook 派特的幸福劇本 by Matthew Quick
(1) Reading: Selected chapters from “The Silver Linings Playbook”
(2) Film: Selected scenes from the film adaptation.  
(3) Focus: Mental health, family, and optimism.  

Week 13: The Kite Runner 追風箏的孩子 by Khaled Hosseini
(1) Reading: Selected chapters from “The Kite Runner”
(2) Film: Selected scenes from the film adaptation.  
(3) Focus: Guilt, redemption, and cross-cultural memory.  

Unit Four: Standing Up for Social Justice  
Week 14: The Help 姊妹 by Kathryn Stockett
(1) Reading: Selected chapters from “The Help”
(2) Film: Selected scenes from the film adaptation.  
(3) Focus: Race, gender, and domestic labor in the US South.

scorePolicy:
Percentile distribution of final grades 評分百分比:
1. Attendance and participation in classroom discussions:  50%
3. Midterm and final oral reports on the novel of your choice: 15% X 2 = 30%
4. Final project (written):  20% to be handed in at the last class


Details of the assessment  percentage 百分比細節 
1. Attendance and participation in class discussions 出席與課堂討論參與：50%
（1）Regular attendance (including being on time).  
（2）Active participation in whole-class and group discussions on the weekly readings and film clips.  
（3）Short in-class tasks (e.g., response notes, group summaries, mini language/culture activities).  

2. Midterm and final oral reports on a selfselected novel 期中與期末口頭報告：15% x 2 = 30%
(1) Midterm oral report (first half of the novel): 15%  
(2) Content: author background, context, brief plot of the first half, main characters, key themes.  
(3) Delivery: 5 minutes per student, plus brief Q&A.  

(1) Final oral report (second half + interpretation/creative work): 15%  
(2) Content: development and ending of the novel, theme analysis, comparison with film (if any), and personal analysis or creative reinterpretation.  
(3) Delivery: 5 minutes per student, plus brief Q&A.  

3. Final written project 期末書面作業：20% 
(1) A short analytical or creative paper (for example: thematic analysis, comparison of novel and film, character study, or creative rewriting from another character’s point of view).  
(2) Suggested length (undergraduate level):  
 Analytical paper: about 1,500–2,000 words.  
 Creative project: equivalent length plus a 500–800 word reflective commentary explaining your choices.  


Weekly Class Time 課堂時間規畫  
A possible weekly structure:  
(1) 50 minutes: Close reading of selected passages (language, narrative techniques, cultural elements).  
(2) 50 minutes: Film clips + guided discussion (adaptation choices, visual storytelling, comparison with text).  
(3) 50 minutes: Student centered activities (small-group discussion, short presentations, group worksheets, preparation for oral reports or written projects).
